title: Fujimori formalizes plan to militarize policing; security experts and Congress voice skepticism
detail: President Fujimori outlined formal plans to deploy the military into prisons and onto the streets to combat criminality and citizen insecurity, though whether the measure would be permanent or time-limited remained unclear. She intends to use the requested 120-day emergency legislative powers to implement the shift by decree. Security specialists expressed skepticism: a former interior minister asked 'Are they going to put troops into every corner store? Are we going to put a soldier in every bus?', noting that previous states of emergency have failed to reduce Peru's rising homicide rate and warning of the risk of increased human-rights violations. Left-of-center parties in Peru's new bicameral Congress said they would seek to impose conditions on the government's legislative-powers request before approving it.

media.caption: Fujimori confirms deployment of the Armed Forces to support police operations
